title: January 2026, Seoul
description:
Eyes open in the dark.

A room where you can touch the ceiling. Four-and-a-half square meters.
Open the window and the next building is close enough to touch.
A goshiwon — a micro-studio — in Sinchon. {name}'s room.

{name}. Thirty-three years old.
Until half a year ago, he was paying off debt.

His father co-signed a loan. The debtor vanished.
The debt fell to the father, and then to {name}.
Age twenty-seven to thirty-three. Six years.

All paid. And what's left — ₩500,000 in the bank, and this room.

choices.text: Slowly pull yourself up
choices.result_text:
Peel back the blanket and stand.
Winter morning light seeps through the small window.
Another day. A day you have to live through.

title: A Call
description:
The phone rings. The screen reads 'Dad'.

A moment's hesitation — then you answer.

"Hey, son. You up?"
"Yeah."

A brief silence. Dad never rehearses what he wants to say.

"...You eat yet?"

Six years in those three words.
Guilt, shame, and everything he can't quite say.

choices.text: "Yeah, I ate. Don't skip meals, Dad."
choices.result_text:
A lie. You haven't eaten anything yet.
But you felt him relax on the other end of the line.
"Good... I'm sorry, son."
"Nothing to be sorry for."
You hung up and stared at the ceiling for a long time.

[Your bond with Dad deepened — relationships are one of the pillars of this game.]

choices.text: "I'm busy. I'll call you back." Click.
choices.result_text:
You cut it short. Longer calls just make the silence hurt more.
You put the phone down and swallowed what you didn't say.
That small hesitation in his voice before you hung up — you couldn't stop thinking about it.

[Your bond with Dad weakened — every choice shapes every relationship.]

title: Gangnam
description:
After the call, {name} opens a worn notebook.

On the very first page, a single line.
The apartment his father spent a lifetime saving for. The one stolen by fraud.
— An apartment in Gangnam.

Dad never brings it up anymore.
{name} never asks.
But they both know what it means.

The doctor told his father: no overexerting yourself.
How much time was left, nobody knew.

{name} writes a number in the notebook.
₩3,000,000,000. Five years.
He knows it's impossible. That's exactly why — he starts.

choices.text: Close the notebook. Stand up.
choices.result_text:
The goal is set.
No plan yet. Not enough money, connections, or time.
But — stop moving and it's over. {name} laced up his shoes.

title: First Meal
description:
Out of the goshiwon, into the convenience store.

You think about the bank balance. ₩500,000.
Next month's goshiwon rent is ₩650,000. Already in the red.

Standing in front of the shelves, {name} does the math.
One triangle kimbap: ₩1,200. Should you even buy it?

Less than ten thousand won to spend each day.
Every meal, every choice — shows up on the bank statement.

This is {name}'s reality right now.

choices.text: Buy a triangle kimbap (-₩1,200)
choices.result_text:
You grab a tuna-mayo and pay.
A little over a thousand won leaves your account.

[Every choice shifts your resources — money, health, mental strength. Every decision has a cost.]

choices.text: Skip it. Save every won.
choices.result_text:
You walk out empty-handed.
Your stomach growled, but the account held.

[Every choice shifts your resources — save money, take the physical hit. Balance is everything.]

title: Can't Wait Any Longer
description:
Two weeks in.

The balance is already shrinking. Income: ₩0.
At this rate you won't last a month.

Another wedding announcement in the old high school group chat.
{name} types 'Congrats' and flips the phone face-down.

One thing is clear:
Something — anything — has to start. Now.
Job hunting. Part-time work. Whatever it takes.

It's {name}'s turn to move.

choices.text: Open a job app. Survival comes first.
choices.result_text:
Convenience store. Delivery. Café. Office temp...
For the first time, 'work' felt like a real option.
{name} hovered a finger over the apply button.

[From here, every month you decide what to do.
On the next screen — make your first move.]

title: Half a Year Gone
description:
Six months in.

I still remember how lost I felt when I first moved into this room.
One suitcase, five hundred thousand won.

Where does {name} stand now?
Better than back then? Or did I just survive it?

Outside the window, Seoul keeps spinning, fast as ever.

choices.text: I held on well. Let's keep going.
choices.result_text:
Half a year.
Small things piled up and carried me this far.
{name} is still here. That's all of it, and that's enough.

choices.text: Still not enough. I need to move faster.
choices.result_text:
A restlessness set in. It isn't a bad thing.
I just have to tighten the screws only as much as I can take without breaking.
{name} knows where that line is.

choices.text: Just rest. Today, at least, I won't think about anything.
choices.result_text:
Half a day of doing nothing.
Guilt rose up, then faded.
Enduring takes stamina too. Today {name} recharged it.

title: A Year Gone
description:
Twelve months.

{name}.

This time last year you unpacked your bags in this room for the first time.
Back then you didn't even know how big Seoul was.

And now?

If you're still in a goshiwon, something feels like it's going wrong;
if you're living in an apartment, you got lucky, or you really did well.
Wherever you are, the fact remains: you survived a year.

How hard it is to hang on in Seoul,
only someone who has hung on truly knows.

choices.text: Just making it this far means something
choices.result_text:
I decided not to compare.
{name} is moving at {name}'s own pace.
Even if that pace looks slow, it isn't a stop.

choices.text: A year passed and I'm still here? Time to burn bright.
choices.result_text:
I lit the flame.
I just hope this energy lasts.
{name} already knows: restlessness and resolve are different things.

title: A Rainy Night
description:
11 p.m. Rain taps against the window.

I grabbed a can of coffee from the vending machine in the goshiwon hallway and came back to my room.
Lying on the bed, I stare at the ceiling.

Did I live today properly?
Do I still remember why I came to Seoul?

{name} quietly closes both eyes.

choices.text: Yeah, one step at a time. I won't give up.
choices.result_text:
One sip of coffee.
I can start over tomorrow.
{name} is still here.

choices.text: I'm worn out. I'll just rest today.
choices.result_text:
Sometimes resting properly beats
forcing yourself to do something and getting nothing done.
{name} learned that today.

title: News from a Friend
description:
A KakaoTalk message came from a high school friend.

'I got into a big company lol'

For a second, as I typed 'congrats,' my fingers froze.

We came to Seoul the same year.
They're at a major firm, and {name} is still...

I tried not to compare. It's harder than I expected.

choices.text: I'm genuinely happy for them. I have my own path.
choices.result_text:
I sent a message of congratulations.
My heart is a little tangled, but that's okay too.
Only {name} can walk {name}'s road.

choices.text: It lit a fire under me. I should work harder.
choices.result_text:
I sent a reply and sat down at my desk.
A night where impatience and will got mixed together.
I hope this feeling doesn't become poison for {name}.

choices.text: Close the SNS app. Now is the time to focus on what's mine.
choices.result_text:
Comparing is a waste of energy.
{name} decided to focus on what {name} can do right now.
Not being shaken by someone else's pace is a skill too.

title: First Paycheck
description:
A notification chimed.

[Deposit] {name}'s account  ₩1,200,000

I stared blankly at the screen.
After taxes and transit costs, it isn't much.
Still, it's money I earned by working.

The first money ever to land in my account under my own name.
A small number, but somehow it moved me.

choices.text: Buy my parents something with my first paycheck
choices.result_text:
I sent a 100,000-won gift card.
'It's fine, save your money,' came the reply.
{name} stared at that text for a long time.

choices.text: Save it all. The future comes before feelings.
choices.result_text:
I left it untouched in the account.
The lump in my throat lasted only a moment. {name} starts preparing for next month.

choices.text: Buy a small gift for myself, who worked so hard
choices.result_text:
A 50,000-won pair of sneakers.
Not expensive, but bought with {name}'s first paycheck.
I think I'll remember this day every time I wear them.

title: First Day at Work
description:
I woke up ten minutes before the alarm.

A new job, my first.
What to wear, how many minutes early to arrive,
whether to eat lunch alone or with others.
Every little thing is a first.

On the subway, {name} stood there in a daze.
Everyone was living their own morning.

Now I'm one of them too.

choices.text: Arrive ten minutes early and survey the place
choices.result_text:
{name} sat alone in an empty office.
It was awkward, but the first impression was made.
These ten minutes might be remembered later.

choices.text: Walk in right on time
choices.result_text:
Punched in exactly on schedule.
Decided not to overthink it.
{name} chose to start simply as {name}.

title: Working Late
description:
10 p.m. Only {name} is left in the office.

When I looked up from the screen under the fluorescent lights,
it was already pitch black outside.

If I don't finish today, it carries over to tomorrow.
Tomorrow might mean another late night.

Somewhere in Seoul, what are my friends doing right now?

choices.text: Finish it and go. Home's just a goshiwon anyway.
choices.result_text:
11:30 p.m. The deadline's met.
I fell asleep the moment I got on the bus.
{name} held on again today.

choices.text: Just clock out today. Tomorrow's work is for tomorrow.
choices.result_text:
I felt the stares, but I left.
The fish-cake broth from the convenience store on the way home was the best part of the day.
{name} gave today back to {name}.

choices.text: Grab one more coffee and push through
choices.result_text:
1 a.m. All done.
The way home was long, but oddly I felt refreshed.
This exhaustion is slowly making {name} a little tougher.

title: Saturday Morning
description:
9 a.m. A day with no alarm.

On weekdays I'd already be on the commuter subway by now.
Today I don't have to do anything.

But doing nothing somehow feels like falling behind.
{name} stares at the ceiling from the bed.
What is this feeling, this guilt that comes from resting?

choices.text: Go to a cafe and study. Time is precious.
choices.result_text: Sat and studied for four hours. It was productive. But I'm a bit tired.

choices.text: Just rest. I'll give this one day to myself.
choices.result_text:
Did nothing. Took only a walk around the neighborhood in the afternoon.
Somehow it felt like next week would go better.

choices.text: Go out to meet a friend
choices.result_text: Laughed for the first time in a while. Living alone in Seoul, this is the hardest thing of all.

title: The Person Next Door
description:
I've lived in the goshiwon for a few months now,
but I still haven't gotten a proper look at the person in the next room.

When we pass in the hallway, we avoid each other's eyes.
Me, and them too.

We're each here for our own reasons,
enduring in our own ways, I suppose.

Today {name} thought about saying hello for the first time.

choices.text: Offer a single 'Hello'
choices.result_text:
'Oh, hi.' A short reply, then they walked off.
But after that, the hallway felt a little less awkward.
{name} figured that was enough.

choices.text: Just pass by. It's easier not to get involved.
choices.result_text:
Eyes down, I walked past.
This is what it means to live alone in Seoul.
{name} is learning that way too now.

title: Payday
description:
Morning of the 25th. On the commuter subway, I opened the app.

Deposit confirmed.
The number in {name}'s account had changed.

After taxes, after rent, I'd already calculated how little would be left.
Still, the fact that a month of work amounted to that number
somehow moved me a little.

choices.text: Save it all. Now is the time to scrimp.
choices.result_text: Left it untouched in the account. Held down the urge. For later.

choices.text: Buy a small gift for myself, who worked so hard
choices.result_text: A 50,000-won pair of sneakers. Not expensive, but bought with my own money.

choices.text: Think about how to grow this money
choices.result_text: I jotted income and expenses in a notes app. I started to see how much I could put toward investing.

title: Thinking of Home
description:
Around the holidays. The news shows crowds heading home.

{name} didn't buy a ticket. No, didn't bother to.
Go home and the questions pour out.
'Got a job yet?' 'Saved any money?' 'How's Seoul?'

Even if Seoul is suffocating,
home isn't ready to take me back yet.

choices.text: Go down anyway. I miss my parents.
choices.result_text:
I ate the meal Mom made.
The questions poured out, but they were bearable.
On the bus back to Seoul, {name} felt strangely lighter.

choices.text: Stay in Seoul this year. This is the right call.
choices.result_text:
I called, at least. Their voice sounded a little lonely.
Spending the holiday alone in a goshiwon
was far lonelier than {name} had expected.

title: I Opened My Bankbook
description:
Today I happened to check my balance.

When I first came to Seoul it was a million won.
Under {name}'s name, the number had changed.

It isn't a huge amount, but it's a number I built.
Eating, sleeping, working, saving, stacking it up.

Gangnam is far off,
but it feels like I've taken one step from the starting line.

choices.text: Protect this money and grow it further
choices.result_text:
Not losing comes first. Growing it comes next.
For the first time, {name} became someone who protects money.

choices.text: It's time to move more aggressively
choices.result_text:
No time to hesitate. Now is the chance.
{name} began preparing the first real bet.

choices.text: Record this moment
choices.result_text:
I wrote the date and the amount in my notes.
I hope I can look back at this number and smile someday.
{name}'s Gangnam Dream began here.

title: A Year and a Half
description:
Eighteen months.

Seoul isn't strange to me anymore.
The commute, the convenience store I frequent, the diner where I have lunch.
It's all familiar now.

But I'm not sure being familiar is a good thing.
Are the things {name} wants still here?
Or is this just becoming the way I live?

I was browsing job listings, then closed the window.

choices.text: Now's the time. Prepare to switch jobs.
choices.result_text:
I pulled out my resume again.
I organized what I'd learned at my current job.
Even if it feels like I'm not ready, the ones who move are the ones who catch the chance.

choices.text: Hold on a bit longer. Build more where I am.
choices.result_text:
Job-hopping later. For now I'll learn more here.
This is a time that needs depth more than haste.
{name} held the position again today.

choices.text: Decide not to think about it now. Just live today.
choices.result_text:
I closed the window and ate.
Some things just don't have an answer right now.
{name} is slowly learning to accept that.

title: Two Years
description:
Twenty-four months.

{name} has become a Seoulite.
Subway transfers, real estate apps, eating lunch in eight minutes flat.

I met my hometown friends for the first time in a while,
and they said my speech had changed a little.
That a Seoul accent had crept in.

Strangely, that made me a little wistful.
And at the same time, it felt like I'd become something.

Two years have passed.

choices.text: Resolve to put down deeper roots in Seoul
choices.result_text:
This became {name}'s city.
Someday I'll build something in this city.
That conviction took root, just a little.

choices.text: The changing me feels strange. Take a quick trip home.
choices.result_text:
I took the train down.
Eating the meal Mom made, I returned to childhood for a moment.
Heading back up to Seoul, {name} felt a little tougher.

title: Three Years
description:
Three years.

Thirty-six.

The people around me are starting to change.
Someone got married, someone bought a house,
someone went abroad to study, someone started a company.

Where is {name} right now?
Gangnam is still far.
But strangely, I don't want to give up.

That's still the reason {name} is here.

choices.text: My path is the right one. Different pace is fine.
choices.result_text:
I decided not to measure myself by someone else's milestones.
{name}'s starting line was different from the start.
Comparing is meaningless. The direction {name} is heading is the right one.

choices.text: I have to move faster. Three years is long enough.
choices.result_text:
The restlessness rose again. This time it has direction.
No time to waste.
{name} shifted up a gear.

choices.text: Do everything I can right where I am
choices.result_text:
Living today properly, rather than some grand strategy.
{name} chose to focus on the cards in hand.
Opportunity comes to those who are ready.

title: Four Years
description:
The fourth year.

Thirty-seven.

Now Seoul feels like home.
Whether I've escaped the goshiwon or am still in it, this city has become {name}'s ground.

These days the question is less 'is this the right path?'
and more 'is this pace enough?'

Gangnam is still far.
But closer than it was two years ago.
That's a fact.

choices.text: Pick up the pace. Move more aggressively.
choices.result_text:
I set down the comfortable choice.
I chose the uncomfortable but growing path.
{name}'s four years carry into the fifth.

choices.text: Stabilizing where I am comes first
choices.result_text:
Before running, I tended to my stamina.
If I collapse, everything starts from scratch.
{name} knows that building a foundation is a strategy too.

title: Thirty-Five
description:
Thirty-five.

{name} knows the weight this age carries in Korean society.
Marriage, owning a home, settling into a career.
People around me ask. Where do you live? Married yet?

{name}'s answer is still being prepared.
Gangnam is the goal. I'm not there yet.

But the saying that opportunities shrink after thirty-five,
{name} has decided not to believe it.

There's still time.

choices.text: This is the most important turning point of my life. Go all in.
choices.result_text:
The skills have stacked up now. The timing is there too.
{name} read thirty-five not as 'not yet' but as 'now.'
There's no age limit on taking a chance.

choices.text: Stay unshaken. Protect my foundation.
choices.result_text:
Whatever anyone says, {name} has {name}'s own pace.
Not collapsing comes first.
From a solid foundation, aim for Gangnam.

title: The Final Half Year
description:
Thirty-eight is right around the corner.

Exactly six months left.

The bank balance, the portfolio, the pay stubs.
{name} looked over the numbers again.

How far is it to a Gangnam apartment?
Is it possible within this half year?

A single choice made this month weighs heavier than any month so far.

choices.text: The last year, pour everything into it
choices.result_text:
Regret can come later.
For now, just go.
{name} laid down every remaining card.

choices.text: Don't push it. What I've done so far is enough
choices.result_text:
Maybe Gangnam isn't everything.
For the first time, {name} truly accepted that thought.

choices.text: There's still a way. Run the numbers again
choices.result_text:
Numbers don't lie.
{name} ran the simulation for the remaining twelve months.
A possibility came into view.
